newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela won't pay ransom for hostages.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela won't pay ransom for hostages.

text.p: The Venezuelan government said on Thursday it was not prepared to pay ransom for two oil workers kidnapped on the Colombian border on Wednesday.

The state oil company engineers were snatched by "presumed guerrilla groups" from oil fields in the southwestern state of Apure and taken to Colombian territory, said a spokesman for Corpoven, a subsidiary of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela.
"The Venezuelan government is not going to pay protection money to Colombian guerrillas," a cabinet minister told Reuters at the Miraflores presidential palace.
"The cabinet was informed of these hostage takings by the Energy Minister Erwin Arrieta and we agreed that we do not pay ransom," he said.
Local Venezuelan ranchers say protection money is habitually paid to guerrilla groups to prevent kidnapping.
"The situation on the border is serious because it affects Corpoven employees as well as ranchers and farmers," the government source said.
Corpoven produces about 140,000 barrels per day of crude from the Apure-Barinas region.
